name: Cylinder head
what: The cylinder head closes the top of the cylinders and houses the combustion chambers, intake and exhaust ports, and valvetrain.
why: It forms the upper part of each combustion chamber and controls the movement of air-fuel mixture into the cylinders and exhaust gases out.
where: It mounts on top of the block, resting on the cylinder head gasket and aligning with the cylinder bores and fluid passages.
installationReason: Lower the cylinder head onto the installed gasket, keeping the combustion chambers and fluid passages aligned with the block.

guide.overview: The cylinder head is an aluminum-alloy casting mounted above the block. It forms the combustion-chamber roof and contains the intake and exhaust ports, valve guides, and the DOHC VTEC valvetrain architecture used by the B16 family.
guide.operation: The intake and exhaust valves are operated by the camshaft and valvetrain assemblies. Air enters through the intake ports, combustion occurs in the chambers above the pistons, and exhaust gases leave through the exhaust ports. The head also routes coolant and lubricating oil through dedicated passages.
